the majority of coastal residents in this small coastal community were concerned about the potential impacts of a seawaters desalination facility on marine ecosystems and the marine economy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

marine users in a small coastal area are concerned about the potential impacts of a seawaters desalination plant on their marine environment, and that their opinions are shaped by how they use the marine ecosystem, and by their gender.
the majority of respondents were highly concerned about the marine impacts of a proposed seawater desal plant and placed high importance on management measures to reduce or offset marine impacts.
local stakeholders are concerned about marine ecosystem impacts and are interested in reducing and off-setting impacts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
local opinions are not shaped by demographic factors, but by how respondents use and value the nearby marine system and by their concerns about the impacts of the new desalting facility.

the marine ecosystem, and the multiple values that coastal residents derive from this resource, are critical to consider when assessing the potential for conflicts over marine resources and when planning and implementing new marine infrastructure.
local stakeholders' perceptions of marine impacts and management measures are critical to the long-term sustainability of the desalination industry and its acceptance by coastal communities.
